- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., +0.30+ in 2–3 days), model underreacts — raise forecast slightly (e.g., +1–2% for next 3–5 days).
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving >2% from 30-day moving average, model tends to overreact — adjust forecast toward MA by 1–2% per day.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often overestimates volatility — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.20) and price is trending up, model may lag — add 0.5–1% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.
